title: Apply for a licence to supply drugs of addiction
summary: This page provides information and requirements for applying for a licence to supply drugs of addiction at a health facility.
intro: If you wish to supply drugs of addiction at your health facility, for example at a licensed nursing home or private health facility, you'll need to apply for a licence.
who_can_apply: The applicant must be fit and proper to be a licensee.
The premises must be appropriate for the supply of drugs of addiction.
The applicant (individual or corporation) must show the Secretary of NSW Health that they meet the requirements.
what_you_need: Application for a Licence to Supply Drugs of Addiction form (PDF)
Details of the applicant and contact person
Full company extract from the Australian Securities and Investment Commission (ASIC), if applicable
Copy of the certificate of incorporation (if applicable)
Copy of the Act incorporating the church or organisation (if applicable)
Copy of the charitable institution status from the Australian Taxation Office (if applicable)
ASIC certificate of registered business name
Details of the uses to be made of the drugs of addiction

how_to_steps.text: Make your payment online at the NSW Health Payment Portal.
Send the completed application form, the required documents and a copy of the payment receipt to the email on the form.

faqs.q: Who can apply for a licence to supply drugs of addiction?
faqs.a: An individual or corporation can apply if they are fit and proper to be a licensee, the premises are appropriate for the supply of drugs of addiction, and they can show the Secretary of NSW Health of the required documentation.

faqs.q: What documents are required for the application?
faqs.a: You need the application form, statutory declaration, fitness and probity check form, details of the applicant, facility details, company extracts (if applicable), and a National Police Check.

faqs.q: How do I pay the application fee?
faqs.a: You must make your payment online at the NSW Health Payment Portal.
